page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number at top left. One block of text: an upper Greek passage across the full width, then parallel blocks of Greek (left) and Latin in smaller italic type (right), then full-width Latin and Greek running on to the foot of the page. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~70 letters]. Hinc factum, ut Lycurgus Rhetor mo-riturus in Metroum ad Quingentorum Senatum se iudicii[?] deferri, cupiens Reipublicae administratae rationem illis reddere. Plutarchus [?] [illegible, ~80 letters] Metroum [illegible, ~40 letters] Lycurgi [illegible, ~50 letters]. Hae autem leges nullius excipitur, sed comprehenduntur omnes quotquot sunt Magistratus, [illegible, ~10 letters], [illegible, ~10 letters], [illegible, ~20 letters]. Est enim [illegible, ~30 letters]. Unde Lysias, [illegible, ~70 letters]. Quomodo autem referendae sint rationes prae-scribebat Lex in hunc modum:
[illegible, ~60 letters]. [illegible, ~30 letters] Rationes ita referunto: Hoc de publico tantum expendi: nihil. Nihil de publico accepit: nihil expendi.

Habes apud Æschinem [illegible, ~40 letters] Κτησιφῶντα, ubi docet etiam eos, qui nihil de publico acceperant, nihil in publicum impenderant, sed tantum ad Rempublicam accesserant. Lege cogi ad referendas rationes [?] apud Lysiam, se scilicet nihil accepisse, nihil expendisse. [illegible, ~90 letters]

Donec autem rationes retulissent suas Magistratus, fuerunt nihil bonorum in suis potitum habebant potestatem, ex hac Lege: Magistratus ne ferendis rationibus obnoxius de suis bonis nil quicquam Diis consecrare, aut appendere: neque testamentum facere. [illegible, ~50 letters]

Legem habes apud Æschinem [illegible, ~20 letters] Κτησιφῶντα. [illegible, ~120 letters]. Non licet quicquam Diis consecrare, aut appendere, nec licet testamentum facere: ratio est, quia ea, quae consecrant, aut appendunt, aut testamento dant legant [?], oppignerata enim sunt Reipublicae, donec rationes retulerint, vtrobique [?] [illegible, ~50 letters]. Atque haec eadem ratio est, cur non liceat [?] in aliam adoptione transfire familiam: Adoptatus enim familiam mutat & Iitatum, & qui iuris erat sui, alieno subiicitur, quod ab eo, qui reddendis rationibus est obnoxius, fieri non potest, nisi in fraudem Reipublicae.

page.notes: Greek text across the page is very blurred and mostly unreadable; it is marked as illegible rather than guessed. Latin of the parallel right-hand column is in smaller italic type and reads with difficulty in places. Doubtful readings are marked [?]: "mo-riturus", "iudicii", "prae-scribebat", "Iitatum" (probably "lituatum" or similar, printed as read), "vtrobique", and the verb in the Greek/Latin sentence about testamento dant. Several Greek lines are unreadable letter by letter, including the opening lines and the Greek citation from Aeschines. Page appears to be from Samuel Petit's Commentarius, page 226.
